reason: The gap holds: no signing identity, certificate, sign command or signing secret exists anywhere in tauri.conf.json or .github/workflows, and a local release bundle carries only the linker ad-hoc signature (Info.plist not bound, no sealed resources), which Gatekeeper reports as 'damaged' once quarantined. Correction to the fix shape: the promised Windows route is no longer available. SignPath Foundation's free OSS tier requires 'an OSI-approved Open Source license without commercial dual-licensing', and PolyForm Strict + commercial (the 23 Sep relicense) fails both conditions, so Windows signing now needs a paid certificate or service. Findings 3 and 4 are per-platform duplicates of this one and should merge into it.
evidence: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:30-46 (no macOS/windows signing blocks); .github/workflows/build.yml:76; scripts/macos-dev-setup.sh:129-134 (dev-only identity); https://signpath.org/terms: 'OSS License: The project must use an OSI-approved Open Source license without commercial dual-licensing for all components.'

reason: Correction on mechanism: 'pricing TBD until v1.0' and a placeholder address are both what the blueprint itself specifies (§6.1), so the TBD pricing is not drift. The real defect is narrower and live-confirmed: vysted.com has Cloudflare nameservers but no MX and no A record, so commercial@vysted.com (the only commercial contact in COMMERCIAL_LICENSE.md and LICENSING.md) cannot receive mail. PolyForm Strict forbids all commercial use, modification and redistribution, so a public release gives would-be licensees no working path.
